The generated model has neither the split gateways nor the separate alternative tasks (M1, M2, M4, M5), so the alternatives are merged or dropped. The guideline targets that structural pattern, not this process's labels.)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description offers an either-or choice between two named ways of carrying out one step (for example 'X or Y'), and both ways continue to the same following step: Model each named way as its own task or path. Place an exclusive gateway before the alternatives to split the flow, with one outgoing branch per alternative. Join the alternative branches with an exclusive gateway before the common next step. Do not drop an alternative, and do not collapse the alternatives into one generic activity.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description offers an either-or choice between two named ways of carrying out one step (for example 'X or Y'), and both ways continue to the same following step

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that an activity follows the receipt of an item or delivery (for example 'upon receiving X, ...'), and it does not describe any message, signal, time or condition that the process waits for: Do not insert an intermediate catch event for the receipt. Connect the preceding activity directly by a sequence flow to the first activity the description gives after the receipt. Use an intermediate catch event only when the description states a wait for an external message, signal, timer or condition.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that an activity follows the receipt of an item or delivery (for example 'upon receiving X, ...'), and it does not describe any message, signal, time or condition that the process waits for

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description lists several activities of a stage with no order stated between them, and the stage or the process ends only after all of those activities are finished: Model a parallel gateway directly after the task that starts the stage or precedes the list. Fork it into one task per listed activity, each as its own task with the action the description gives for it. Connect every one of those tasks into a second parallel gateway that joins them. Place the join before the next step or the end event, and connect it onward from there. Do not chain the unordered activities in sequence, and do not use an exclusive gateway for either the fork or the join.
rules_sent_back.situation: The description lists several activities that follow one step with no order stated between them, and one of those listed activities is itself given as an either-or choice between two ways joined by 'or' (for example, placing an item in one of two destinations).
